findings.claim: bypass_actors not asserted during verification: creation payload correctly sets bypass_actors=[] but the three-assertion verification block never inspects .bypass_actors; a stale or manually-edited ruleset with non-empty bypass_actors passes all assertions and the applier exits 0, producing a false-assurance ✓.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L85: payload includes bypass_actors: []. L92-131: verification asserts enforcement (L112-116), rule_types (L118-123), include_match (L125-130) — no assertion reads .bypass_actors anywhere. Scenario: admin adds a bypass actor via GitHub API or Settings UI (e.g., a service account or GitHub Actions App to accommodate a CI use-case); operator re-runs applier; existing_id found at L56-58 → creation skipped (no-op branch); L99-130 verification reads full ruleset detail and passes all three assertions; script logs 'tag-protection ruleset present (id=...) ✓' and exits 0. The bypass actor persists undetected. docs/DECISIONS.md D-034 row explicitly states bypass_actors is empty as a design invariant; the verification gap directly undermines the auditability of that invariant.
findings.impact: A non-empty bypass_actors list allows named actors (an OAuth App, a GitHub Actions installation, or a user) to force-push, delete, or update renovate/v* tags, re-enabling the exact supply-chain poisoning scenario CRIT-SAFE-001 was built to prevent. The ✓ log gives the operator false confidence that the invariant holds. In the single-operator estate the admin is the only person who could add a bypass actor, so this is primarily a drift-detection gap rather than a remote-exploit vector. Severity: MIN.
findings.mitigation: Add to verification block after existing assertions: bypass_count=$(printf '%s' "$detail" | jq '.bypass_actors | length'); if [ "$bypass_count" != "0" ]; then echo "verification failed: ruleset id=${final_id} has ${bypass_count} bypass_actors (expected 0)" >&2; exit 1; fi. Update L133 log line to include bypass_actors=0 in the summary string. This gives the D-034 invariant a machine-enforceable check, not just a prose assertion.

findings.claim: conditions.ref_name.exclude not verified: creation payload sets exclude:[] but verification checks only that the expected pattern is present in the include array; a non-empty exclude list that carves out the target pattern renders the ruleset a no-op while verification passes.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L78: payload sets ref_name: { include: [$pattern], exclude: [] }. L125-130: verification checks .conditions.ref_name.include | index($pattern) — if ≠ -1, assertion passes. No statement reads .conditions.ref_name.exclude at any point in the verification block. Scenario: an admin or API-level actor adds exclude:["refs/tags/renovate/v*"] to the ruleset's ref_name conditions (e.g., attempting to carve out a deployment automation). The include array still contains refs/tags/renovate/v*; verification's index check returns 0 (found); script exits 0. But GitHub evaluates the ref_name condition as include ∩ ¬exclude — the exclude overrides the include, and every tag that was supposed to be protected is now explicitly excluded. The ruleset is a no-op.
findings.impact: A non-empty exclude list silently defeats the tag-protection without touching the include array that verification checks. This is a more subtle bypass than bypass_actors because there is no UI affordance that makes adding an exclude pattern feel consequential. Severity: MIN — requires deliberate admin-level modification; initial creation is correct; drift detection gap only.
findings.mitigation: Add to verification block: exclude_count=$(printf '%s' "$detail" | jq '.conditions.ref_name.exclude | length'); if [ "$exclude_count" != "0" ]; then echo "verification failed: ruleset id=${final_id} has ${exclude_count} exclude conditions (expected 0)" >&2; exit 1; fi.

findings.claim: head -1 on name-filtered listing produces non-deterministic ID selection when duplicate-name rulesets exist; both the idempotency check and the verification step may operate on a different (weaker) ruleset than intended.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L56-57: existing_id=$(printf '%s' "$rulesets" | jq -r --arg name "$RULESET_NAME" '.[] | select(.name == $name) | .id' | head -1). L101-102: final_id=$(... same pattern ... | head -1). GitHub Rulesets listing endpoint (GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets) returns an array in unspecified order — the GitHub API documentation does not guarantee sort stability between calls. Scenario: an API-admin-level actor pre-creates a second ruleset named scp-tag-protection-renovate-v with enforcement=disabled or bypass_actors=[<actor>]. On the next applier run: L56-57 finds existing_id non-empty (the weak ruleset's ID or the strong one's, depending on listing order) → creation is skipped. L101-102 final_id = whichever the listing returns first; L109 reads that ruleset's detail; if the listing returns the weak one first, all three assertions may pass against it (enforcement=disabled would fail, but bypass_actors or exclude gaps already documented mean there are other ways to have a passing-but-weak ruleset). The correct ruleset's state is never verified.
findings.impact: Requires API-admin access to pre-create the duplicate. High bar in single-operator estate. However the fix (capture POST response ID) is low-cost and eliminates the class of ambiguity entirely. Severity: MIN.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred): capture the ruleset ID from the POST response to avoid re-listing. Replace the POST call and subsequent final_id lookup with: create_response=$(printf '%s' "$payload" | gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/rulesets" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" --input -); final_id=$(printf '%s' "$create_response" | jq -r '.id'). The POST response body contains the created ruleset's ID; use it directly for the per-ruleset detail fetch in verification. Option B: add a duplicate-count assertion before both head -1 calls: match_count=$(... jq ... | wc -l | tr -d ' '); if [ "$match_count" -gt 1 ]; then echo "ambiguous: ${match_count} rulesets named ${RULESET_NAME}" >&2; exit 1; fi.

findings.claim: target field not verified: verification does not assert .target == "tag"; a ruleset with target=branch and the same name passes all three assertions and produces a ✓ log, but the tag-protection is absent.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L73: payload includes target: "tag". L92-131: verification asserts enforcement, rule-type set, and include-pattern — .target is not read at any point. A branch-targeting ruleset with the same name scp-tag-protection-renovate-v would pass all three assertions. In practice the ref_name include-pattern refs/tags/renovate/v* on a branch ruleset (whose refs are under refs/heads/) would match no refs and be inert — silent no-op rather than active bypass.
findings.impact: Theoretical only — inert branch ruleset with tags-namespace include-pattern fires on no refs, so protection is absent but not actively circumvented. Nit severity; complete verification defence-in-depth warrants the one-line fix.
findings.mitigation: Add: target_val=$(printf '%s' "$detail" | jq -r '.target // "unknown"'); if [ "$target_val" != "tag" ]; then echo "verification failed: ruleset id=${final_id} target=${target_val} (expected tag)" >&2; exit 1; fi.

findings.claim: Post-merge runbook hardcodes operator-local absolute filesystem path /Users/amplience/Projects/scp-track1; non-portable for any future second-maintainer, increasing the risk that the protection-application step is skipped and the protect-then-tag ordering established by NEW-R2-SAFE-001 closure is violated.
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020f/DISPATCH-NOTE.md L73: 'cd /Users/amplience/Projects/scp-track1'. This path is specific to the current operator's machine. DISPATCH-NOTE.md is the canonical operational runbook for this slice (probe 7 scope). A future second-maintainer following the runbook verbatim would receive 'cd: /Users/amplience/Projects/scp-track1: No such file or directory' and would be blocked at the first line before executing the protection script. Likely failure mode: (a) skip step 1 (protection) and go directly to step 2 (git tag + push) — re-introduces the TOCTOU window that NEW-R2-SAFE-001 closed; (b) run steps out of order from memory with no reference to the correct sequence. The runbook also lacks a prerequisite reminder to verify 'gh auth status' with admin scope before invoking the idempotent script, which the script itself requires (L41-43 require_cmd gh but does not validate auth scope).
findings.impact: Safety property of the NEW-R2-SAFE-001 fix (protect-before-tag) is operationally fragile: it depends on the operator reading and correctly executing a runbook that fails at line 1 on any machine other than /Users/amplience. In single-operator estate this is an accepted bus-factor-1 risk, but DISPATCH-NOTE is named as the canonical runbook for future maintainer handoff. MIN.
findings.mitigation: Replace L73 with portable path discovery: 'cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" # navigate to your local SCP checkout root'. Add a prerequisite stanza immediately before the code block: 'Prerequisites: (1) gh auth status — must be authenticated with admin scope on the SCP repo; (2) local main branch is up to date post-squash-merge (git log --oneline -1 should show this slice's merge commit).' Optionally add a final verification command after step 2: 'gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-/rulesets --jq ".[] | select(.name == \"scp-tag-protection-renovate-v\") | {id, enforcement, target}"' so the operator can confirm protection is active before the tag goes live in Renovate's scheduling window.

probe_results.probe_1_jq_arg_safety: SAFE with one nuance. jq -n --arg name "$RULESET_NAME" --arg pattern "refs/tags/$TAG_PATTERN" structurally separates env-var values from JSON syntax: --arg always produces a string-typed JSON value and jq JSON-encodes any embedded quotes, braces, or control chars. The shell string concatenation 'refs/tags/$TAG_PATTERN' expands TAG_PATTERN before the value reaches --arg; this is data concatenation at the shell layer, not JSON injection — jq never sees the raw $TAG_PATTERN expansion, only the fully concatenated string as an opaque arg value. Residual nuance: if TAG_PATTERN contains bash command-substitution tokens (backtick or $(...)), the shell expands them before passing to jq. Both RULESET_NAME and TAG_PATTERN are operator-controlled env vars; operator-level access already implies arbitrary shell execution. This is an accepted trust boundary. No new finding.
probe_results.probe_2_duplicate_name_rulesets: FINDING — see NEW-R3-SAFE-003. Both the idempotency check (L56-57) and the verification step (L101-102) use head -1 on a name-filtered listing; the GitHub Rulesets listing endpoint does not guarantee stable sort order. A pre-existing duplicate-name ruleset with weaker properties causes non-deterministic ID selection, potentially leading the applier to verify the wrong ruleset. Mitigation: capture the POST response ID directly, eliminating the listing re-query dependency for the success path.
probe_results.probe_3_assertions_necessary_sufficient: PARTIAL. enforcement=active, rule-type set, and include-pattern presence are all necessary assertions. Three material gaps remain: (a) bypass_actors not checked — an actor on the bypass list circumvents all three rules (NEW-R3-SAFE-001, MIN); (b) conditions.ref_name.exclude not checked — a non-empty exclude list can negate the include-pattern, rendering the ruleset a no-op (NEW-R3-SAFE-002, MIN); (c) target not checked — a branch-targeting ruleset passes all assertions but protects no tags (NEW-R3-SAFE-004, nit). Of the three, bypass_actors and exclude are materially security-relevant; target is theoretical.
probe_results.probe_4_post_merge_race_window: SAFE. The protect-then-tag reordering (NEW-R2-SAFE-001 closure) eliminates the material window. No automation with write access to the renovate/v* tag namespace exists in this estate: Mend-hosted Renovate Bot creates branch refs (refs/heads/renovate/...) for dependency-bump PRs but never creates tag refs; no GitHub Actions workflow in this repo contains steps that push renovate/v* tags. The inter-command window is seconds on a single-operator manual run; only a compromised PAT in the operator's active shell session could interleave. Practical risk is negligible. No new finding.
probe_results.probe_5_bypass_actors_d034: GAP — confirmed as NEW-R3-SAFE-001. Creation payload at L85 correctly sets bypass_actors: []. D-034 decision row explicitly names bypass_actors=[] as a design invariant. Verification block at L92-131 reads enforcement, rule_types, and include_match but never reads .bypass_actors. Re-running the applier after an admin adds a bypass actor via the GitHub API or Settings UI exits 0 with a false-assurance ✓ log. The invariant stated in D-034 has no machine-enforced check. Two-line jq assertion closes it.
probe_results.probe_6_ruleset_overlap: NO OVERLAP — confirmed. GitHub Repository Rulesets use fnmatch-style glob matching where the wildcard * does NOT match / (the path-separator character), consistent with POSIX fnmatch(3) FNM_PATHNAME semantics. refs/tags/v* therefore matches refs/tags/v<any-non-slash-sequence> — e.g. refs/tags/v1.0.0 matches but refs/tags/renovate/v1.0.0 does NOT match because the renovate/ segment contains a slash before the v. The two rulesets cover disjoint namespaces; the script header assertion at L6-10 is correct. Minor documentation gap: no citation to GitHub's ref-pattern glob semantics is present in the header comment or branch-protection.md; a future maintainer questioning the non-overlap claim would have to verify empirically. Nit only; no safety finding.
probe_results.probe_7_runbook_completeness: PARTIALLY COMPLETE for current operator; NOT COMPLETE for a future second-maintainer. The protect-then-tag sequence is operationally correct and the rationale comment is clear. Two gaps: (1) L73 hardcodes /Users/amplience/Projects/scp-track1 — a second-maintainer following the runbook fails immediately (NEW-R3-SAFE-005, MIN); (2) no prerequisite check for gh auth admin scope is stated — the script requires admin scope but the runbook does not prompt the operator to verify this before running. Step 3 ('Open the follow-up PR pinning renovate.json to the new tag') is underprescribed; the extends format and expected renovate.json diff are not shown, which is acceptable for the current operator (TF-020F-001 provides context) but would require additional lookup for an onboarding second-maintainer.
probe_results.probe_8_dependabot_note: VERIFIED CLOSED. DISPATCH-NOTE.md L57-66 verification artefact block explicitly states: 'Dependabot PRs are NOT corroborating evidence because Dependabot is GitHub-native, not Mend-hosted.' FIX-ROUND-2.md's claim is confirmed accurate — the note is present in DISPATCH-NOTE.md, not only in FIX-ROUND-2.md. No finding.

structured_review.summary: R3 safety/bypass review of 020F post fix-round-2. Both R2 MINs confirmed closed: NEW-R2-SAFE-001 (TOCTOU) closed by protect-then-tag reordering in DISPATCH-NOTE.md (step 1 now applies ruleset, step 2 cuts and pushes tag); NEW-R2-SAFE-002 (heredoc injection + weak verification) closed by jq --arg construction and three-assertion verification block. No new CRIT or MAJ findings. Five new findings: NEW-R3-SAFE-001 (MIN) — bypass_actors never asserted in verification; re-running applier after admin adds a bypass actor silently exits 0, undermining the D-034 invariant; two-line jq assertion closes it. NEW-R3-SAFE-002 (MIN) — conditions.ref_name.exclude never verified; a non-empty exclude list negates the include-pattern and renders the ruleset a no-op while all three assertions pass; two-line fix. NEW-R3-SAFE-003 (MIN) — head -1 on name-filtered listing is non-deterministic when a duplicate-name ruleset pre-exists; capturing the POST response ID eliminates the ambiguity. NEW-R3-SAFE-004 (nit) — target field not asserted; branch-targeting ruleset with same name would be inert but pass verification. NEW-R3-SAFE-005 (MIN) — post-merge runbook hardcodes /Users/amplience/Projects/scp-track1; non-portable for a future second-maintainer, creating operational risk that the protect-then-tag ordering is skipped. All five findings are addressable in the same follow-up PR as TF-020F-001. Merge-unblocked. LGTM_WITH_CONDITIONS.
